title: Protection Officer - Monitoring
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Protection Officer - Monitoring for our operations in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

Under the technical supervision of the Protection Manager, the Protection officer (Monitoring), will implement protection monitoring activities in the target locations. Specifically, the role will plan and conduct protection monitoring visits in the communities, through data collection and encoding, referral of individuals at risk, information sharing, and timely reporting on protection trends and risks identified. The position will, furthermore, be tasked to identify and provide direct assistance and support to people with specific needs. Additionally, the position is expected to contribute to other protection activities that DRC is implementing in the area.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:


	Develop a work plan for the implementation of protection monitoring activities in the identified sites.
	Ensure protection monitoring activities are implemented in line with international standards, best practices and DRC protection monitoring guidelines
	Carry out the protection monitoring activities according to work plan and allocated budget
	Contribute in the development and review of protection monitoring tools and in the analysis of the collected information
	Undertake data collection using the standardized tools (Key Information Interviews, Focus Group Discussion and observation)
	Collaborate closely with all sectors to ensure that information gathering and reporting are integrated across the board
	Collaborate with the protection manager country PM specialist in reviewing protection trends and needs in DRC’s areas of intervention and recommend appropriate responses for DRC’s and other agencies
	Conduct service and resource mapping to determine available services and ensure effective protection services and referrals
	Support Identification of individuals with specific needs and referral to relevant services including Individual Protection Assistance.
	Collaborate with relevant partners to develop and maintain protection referral mechanisms.
	Conduct community awareness raising and information dissemination on identified protection risks and prevention and mitigation strategies;
	Ensure the continuity of protection programming (case management, referrals) and the identification of cases through protection monitoring.
	Hold regular meetings with community-based groups/networks and help establish 'community action plans' to address protection risks.
	Maintain good professional relationships with other stakeholders to collect daily information on protection and support safe referrals
	Mobilize and create strong rapport with communities through engaging with community-based structures on a consistent basis and sticking to respectful, culturally appropriate ways.
	Support community-based structures through promoting meaningful group conversation and guiding members to self-identify community protection concerns.
	Engage in developing and implementing response plans according to the finding of protection monitoring with the leadership of protection manager;
	Represent DRC in engagement with the target community and their representatives, local gov’t structures, humanitarian and development agencies operating in the target area with the guidance and leadership of the protection manager.
	Work with other DRC sectoral staff to encourage referrals and information exchange.
	Ensure ethical and statistically-sound data collection, analysis and protection


Report writing and documentation 


	Meet with the Community based protection officer and protection community workers on a weekly basis for individual support
	Contribute to producing monthly and quarterly protection monitoring reports and ad hoc briefs
	Support in the development of daily, weekly and monthly reports.
	Ensure proper documentation of all project activities including means of verification, assessments and case studies.
	Contribute to the development of project proposal and concept notes. 


Experience and technical competencies:


	Minimum of 3 years’ experience in an entry to mid-level position, with experience in the field of humanitarian response, development response, research and refugee/IDP protection working for an international NGO, UN agency or relevant ministry or local authority.
	Strong communication skills in both English and the local languages; ability to conduct interviews, facilitate discussions, and write reports in English.
	Experience in conducting protection monitoring or protection assessments using online data collection tools such as Kobo and Activity info
	Good data c

title: Protection and Peacebuilding Officer
Community Mobilizer
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a qualified Community Mobilizer for our operations in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

The Community Mobilizer will support the implementation of DRC’s mixed migration project by engaging with communities and people on the move, disseminating relevant protection and legal information, identifying protection concerns, facilitating referrals, and strengthening community participation and linkages with available services along the migration routes. 

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:


	Conduct regular outreach and information sessions with migrants, returnees, host communities and other people on the move at targeted locations.
	Disseminate clear and accessible information on legal rights and duties, available protection and legal aid services, case management, PSS, civil documentation, safe and regular migration pathways, and risks associated with irregular migration;
	Support the Protection Team in writing weekly/monthly reports with analyses of identified and counselled vulnerable cases;
	Engage women, girls, persons with disabilities and other groups who may face additional barriers to accessing information and service, and risk identification and mitigation;
	Conduct risk assessment visits to identify risks faced by target populations and mitigate these risks through collaboration with protection team, arrange referrals to other partners, provision of in-house services and advocacy;
	Identification and referrals for case management and other specialized services;
	Collect and communicate community feedback, concerns and suggestions to the project and protection teams for appropriate follow-up
	Maintain close relation with key stakeholders and other protection actors, and regularly inform on protection incident and trends;
	Maintain good working relations with implementing partners, community structures and local authorities;
	Set up necessary measures and create a conducive work environment to ensure confidentiality during interviews and to secure sensitive information;
	Deliver capacity building and best practice messages to the community;


Community Based Protection and Participation


	Support the establishment, strengthening and engagement of community-based protection structures, networks or focal points along the targeted migration routes.



	Support communities/CBPNs to identify and prioritize protection risks and develop appropriate community-led actions and solutions.
	Facilitate community consultations and participation in protection activities, ensuring meaningful participation of women, men, youth, persons with disabilities and other potentially excluded groups.
	Support community-based protection structures through awareness sessions, mentoring and capacity-building activities as guided by the Protection Team.


 Monitoring, Reporting and Accountability


	Maintain accurate records of outreach, information sessions, referrals, community feedback and other assigned activities while ensuring confidentiality.
	Support regular collection of field-level information on protection concerns, service availability, access barriers and emerging trends.
	Provide timely inputs for weekly, monthly and other project reports.
	Work closely with the M&E team to support monitoring of project activities and collection of quality data.
	Support accountability to affected populations by ensuring that communities are informed about available services, feedback mechanisms and their rights to provide feedback or raise concerns.
	Ensure that community engagement and service delivery are inclusive, gender- and disability-sensitive, and accessible to different groups


Experience and technical competencies:


	Experience working with migrants, returnees, refugees, IDPs, host communities or other vulnerable and mobile populations is highly desirable and practical experience in mobilization and awareness-raising.
	Up to 1 year experience working with vulnerable communities, basic needs and distribution programming experience, local authority capacity building and/or advocacy programmes.
	Experience in engaging with communities, including organizing, mobilizing, and facilitating awareness-raising sessions.
	Experience with NGO’s, UN, etc, highly regarded.
	Interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to establish effective working relations with local and international staff and other stakeholders;


EDUCATION: (include certificates, licenses, etc.)


	Grade 12 certificate or relevant training, with moderate technical skills

	Proficiency in English is essential

title: Protection Officer – Protection Case Management
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Protection Officer – Protection Case Management for our operations in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

Under the supervision of the Protection Project Manager, the Protection Case Management Officer will implement the protection case management activities in line with international standards, best practices and DRC protection case management SOP. The incumbent is expected to conduct regular service mapping, coordination with actors, particularly those working on the migration issues including the national and regional sub-national partnership coalition members, UN Agencies, INGOs, and Local CSOs providing service for people on the move. The protection case management officer is expected to provide timely and comprehensive case management services primarily for those individuals on the move and facing protection risks by coordinating essential services.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:


	Implement protection case management activities in line with the global protection cluster guideline, best practices and DRC protection case management Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
	Conduct identification, assessment, planning, intervention and follow-up for professional case management in support of vulnerable beneficiaries

	Coordinate with other DRC Country Office case management team and provide timely cross-boarder case management service for people on the move requiring the service
	Conduct case conference with other actors working on migration for complex cases to ensure that timely action is taken to provide immediate and comprehensive support
	Facilitate cash for protection (C4P) as part of the protection case management to ensure that people on the move who are facing imminent protection risk(s) can access life-saving protection services

	Ensure that the protection case management service is provided in a rights-based approach, by making sure that the service is neither promoting nor preventing migration.

title: Information Management Officer - Protection
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Information Management Officer - Protection for our operations in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

Under the supervision of the Program Development and Quality Manager (PDQM) the Protection Information Management (PIM) Officer will be supporting the overall quality of protection-related data management across DRC Ethiopia’s projects. To this end, she or he will play a critical role in supporting the execution of day-to-day activities related to information management through the collection, analysis and sharing of information in a sensitive and appropriate way in accordance with professional standards for protection work. She or he will be responsible for contributing to the overall maintenance of various PIM related tools, ensuring support to field teams to improve the quality of protection data, and timely protection analysis and reporting. The PIM Officer will also support the PIM Specialist and the Protection Coordinator to improve the collection, storage, and analysis of protection information to support the development of evidence-based protection interventions and measuring the impact of protection projects.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:


	Support in developing and maintaining DRC Ethiopia’s protection database and MEAL information management systems.
	Support in the rollout of standardized protection databases and information management systems across DRC Ethiopia’s protection activities, including for the case management and protection monitoring.
	Support the maintenance of databases of confidential information and ensure there is provision for data security, including strict data handling and confidentiality protocols, weekly backup and recovery control.
	Develop and maintain an inventory of relevant documents on the humanitarian situation of Ethiopia, including mission reports, assessments and evaluations.
	Process data, compile and disseminate information for use in various protection-related materials, including but not limited to reports, briefings, analyses
	Ensure timely and high-quality of protection reporting for both internal and external audiences
	Provide support to the Protection Specialist (Monitoring and Analysis) in the maintenance and development of various KOBO forms, ActivityInfo and support field teams in collecting relevant data.
	Develop various data collection tools both for protection and MEAL teams using digital platforms such as Kobo toolbox and Activity Info and support field teams in collecting relevant data using digital platforms
	Lead the adoption and use of data analytics and visualization including Advanced Excel, power BI and Tableau
	Ensure compliance with data protection and security procedures and policies as per DRC policies, including strict data handling and confidentiality protocols, weekly backup and recovery control.
	Conduct field visits to monitor PIM activities and provide capacity-building in line with core PIM competencies
	Provide remote support to strengthen data collection, analysis, and reporting in hard-to-reach locations with communication challenges
	Enhance DRC staff’s knowledge and capacity to use relevant databases and in topics including data quality, and basic data analysis
	Support with general information management priorities of the DRC Ethiopia office as requested by the Protection Coordinator, MEAL Team, PDQM and Head of Program 


Experience and technical competencies:


	At least 3 years of experience with an NGO or UN agency, at least 2 years of which should be in an operational setting.
	Experience in developing, managing information, and using databases in humanitarian settings.
	Experience compiling information for external dissemination.
	Good experience in research and data/information management, information security as well as quality assurance techniques.
	Strong understanding of humanitarian, displacement and protection issues.
	Strong knowledge of Excel and MS Access or other databases, SharePoint online, and other modern tools.
	Strong knowledge of data collection, analysis and visualization tools and techniques, such as ActivityIfo, Kobo, Power-BI, PivotTables/charts, google forms, among others.
	Previous experience working with protection-related databases and information systems including creating and maintaining ActivityInfo, CPIMS+, GBVIMS+ etc desired.

	Relevant bachelor’s degree or qualification in information systems, communications, social sciences or related field


LANGUAGE: (indicate Fluency level)


	Excellent proficiency in written and spoken English and other local langua

title: Peacebuilding Officer
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a qualified Peacebuilding Officer for our operations in Jigjiga/Dre Dawa, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

The Peacebuilding Officer will be responsible for implementing activities related to conflict resolution, peacebuilding, and community engagement aimed at promoting peace, reconciliation, and social cohesion along the eastern migration route, with a focus on Jigjiga, Dire Dawa, and Togochale. The role holder will work closely with stakeholders at regional, woreda, kebele, and community levels, as well as community leaders and project partners, to facilitate dialogue, build relationships, and support sustainable peacebuilding initiatives. He/she will also be responsible for organizing peace dialogues at woreda and community levels, monitoring progress and impact, and contributing to positive social change.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:


	Supporting the peacebuilding component of projects, overseeing project activities, budgets, and reporting
	Conduct participatory conflict and conflict sensitivity analyses through community consultations and participatory processes to identify and prioritize the drivers of instability and opportunities for positive peace outcomes
	Establish peace building committees (including women and young people, IDPs/returnees/host) and provide training on negotiation, mediation and non-violent conflict resolution
	Support CSOs, groups, initiatives, and local change makers promoting peace and social cohesion and responding to conflict displacement with skills reinforcement on dialogue building and conflict prevention/management/resolution
	Facilitate and support community peace-building dialogue forums (local and regional gatherings)
	Ensuring smooth coordination with authorities, security providers, and other organizations to avoid duplication of activities.
	Monitoring, reporting, and evaluating project implementation, including data collection, maintaining monitoring forms, submitting reports and produce success stories


Experience and technical competencies:


	A strong team worker;
	Aptitude to work in difficult conditions and stressful situations;
	Excellent internal and external communication and coordination capabilities and excellent team building and coordination skills;
	Continuous Learning; a colleague who promotes continuous learning for self and others;
	Creativity and Initiative; someone who actively seeks new ways of improving programs, services and partnerships;
	Performance Management; a person who identifies ways and implements actions to improve the performance of self and others;
	Self-motivated and able to work with a minimum of guidance and supervision;
	Experience and technical competencies:
	BSc or MSC degree in Peace Studies, Law, Conflict Management, Social Studies, or related fields.
	Minimum 3 years of professional experience in conflict and peacebuilding which at least for 2 years in an NGO setting.
	Strong knowledge and experience of working in conflict-prone and insecure areas
	Experience working with people on the move, including migrants, returnees, refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons
	Fluency in written and spoken English, as well as fluency in the local language, is mandatory.
	Strong coordination, representation, and interpersonal skills, along with a high degree of computer literacy.


EDUCATION: (include certificates, licenses, etc.)


	BSc or MSc  degree in Peace Studies, Law, Conflict Management, Social Studies


LANGUAGE: (indicate Fluency level)


	Full Proficiency in English language
	Knowledge of the  local language. 


In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies: 

Striving for excellence: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process. 

Collaborating: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback. 

Taking the lead: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation. 

Communicating: You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

title: MEAL Partnership Specialist
description:
MEAL Partnership Specialist

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world’s leading NGOs, with a focus on responding to displacement, have been registered in Sudan since 2004, delivering life-saving programming in protection, emergency response, shelter, food security and livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, camp management, and humanitarian mine action. DRC has implemented projects in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Port Sudan, and White Nile. Sudan hosts one of the largest displaced populations in Africa, with over 3.7 million internally displaced people and over 1.1 million refugees from South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central African Republic, Chad, Yemen and Syria. Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

POSITION PROFILE

The overall purpose of the role:

The MEAL Partnership Specialist supports the strengthening of Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) systems and practices of DRC’s local partners, including national NGOs, CBOs, and volunteer groups such as Emergency Response Rooms and Mutual Aid Groups. 

Working under the supervision of the MEAL Manager and in close coordination and technical guidance from the Partnership Manager/ Partnership Coordinator, the role provides tailored technical support to partners in developing MEAL frameworks, data collection tools, partners’ IPTTs, FCM and reporting systems while ensuring compliance with DRC MEAL standards and donor requirements.

The position focuses on improving data quality, verification of Means of Verification (MoVs), capturing and sharing lessons learnt, and accuracy of reporting practices, including consolidation of indicators in the indicators in the Indicator Performance Tracking Table (IPTT). It also contributes to strengthening partners’ capacities and promoting the use of the data for accountability, learning and program design and improvement.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Support to Local Partners:


	In collaboration with partners and under the guidance of the MEAL Manager, support the design of a logical framework, indicators and MEAL workplans for partner implemented projects.
	Provide ongoing technical support to partner MEAL focal points in developing and reviewing data collection tools for surveys, assessments, and monitoring activities in line with DRC MEAL standards and donor requirement.
	Work closely with Area Office teams to support partners in developing their workplans aligned with agreed objectives and implementation timelines.
	Ensue partners implement verification exercises in line with DRC MEAL SOPs and guidelines.
	Review Means of Verification (MoVs) submitted by partners to ensure quality, completeness, and compliance with project requirements.
	Conduct regular follow-ups with partner organizations to support accurate and timely reporting of achievements.
	Support the documentation and consolidation of reported indicators in the IPTT and ensure alignment with approved logframes.
	Collaborate with partners during planning and implementation of assessments such as baselines, PDMs, and end-lines.
	Reviews partner reports (narrative and MEAL related sections), provide technical feedback and follow up on identified gaps or inconsistencies.


Capacity Strengthening:


	Conducts MEAL Due Diligence (DD) assessments of partners during the onboarding to identify gaps in systems, tools and capacities.
	Contribute to the  development and lead on the implementation of partners capacity building plan from MEAL perspective through technical support for each partner as per their assigned tier (1,2 or 3) resulted from the MEAL DD.
	Conduct targeted coaching and on-the-job mentoring for partner MEAL staff in data collection, quality assurance, and analysis techniques.
	Assist partners in aligning their monitoring tools and methodologies with DRC MEAL minimum operating procedures (MOPs) and donor expectations.
	Facilitate learning and knowledge sharing across partners to improve MEAL practice and use of data.


Monitoring and Evaluation:


	Participate in joint monitoring visits with programme, operations and partner teams as per the agreed monitoring plan.
	Support partners in digital data collection (e.g., KoboToolbox) and ensure a proper data management practices.
	Ensure harmonization and alignment of Scope of work, IPTTs, MEAL Framework, and data collection processes across different partners and sectors.
	Conduct data quality checks, including validation and triangulation of partner reported data against field observations and other sources.
	Identify data inconsistencies and follow up with partners to ensure corrective action are taken


Accountability and Learning:


	Support partners in integrating accountability mechanisms (Community feedback Mechanism and Information sharing), in coordination with the accountability team and Area Office ma

title: Roving Mixed Migration Project Manager

The role provides leadership in ensuring project activities are implemented in line with DRC’s Mixed Migration Policy and Guidelines, donor requirements, and national frameworks, while responding to the evolving needs of refugees, asylum seekers, returnees, IDPs, and other people on the move.

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world’s leading NGOs, with a focus on responding to displacement, have been registered in Sudan since 2004, delivering life-saving programming in protection, emergency response, shelter, food security and livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, camp management, and humanitarian mine action. DRC has implemented projects in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Port Sudan, and White Nile. Sudan hosts one of the largest displaced populations in Africa, with over 3.7 million internally displaced people and over 1.1 million refugees from South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central African Republic, Chad, Yemen and Syria. Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

POSITION PROFILE

The overall purpose of the role:

The Supply Chain Assistant Logistics’ main objective is to provide support in the Supply chain department in efficient and effective Logistics implementation and smooth running of departmental operations of capital office with emphasis

support logistics staff and functions including implementation of DRC Dynamics. The role expected to contribute to strengthen the overall supply chain functions. This position will also ensure implementation of audit recommendation related to logistics.

The post holder will be expected to assist the Supply Chain team leader in fixed asset, and fleet management and ensuring that all logistics operations are managed and maintained in an efficient manner as per DRC’s internal and donor procedure & as per the Operations Handbook..
